result.title: Persistent Memory and Iterative Improvement in an LLM Agent for Chinese-Character Drawing
result.summary: Does persistent memory accumulated from previous attempts help an LLM agent solve new problems, and does memory design affect that benefit? We study programmatic Chinese-character drawing across five agent conditions attempting the same 668 items. Accumulated memory produces modest aggregate gains despite substantial growth in the memory stores: free-form notes improve first-attempt success by 4.6 percentage points, while a design combining free-form memory with reusable code improves it by 2.8 points. The two designs do not differ significantly overall, but the code bank shows a suggestive advantage on later, harder items. A separate post-hoc comparison finds a much larger improvement when the code-bank agent receives privileged, target-specific structural supervision. The agent can therefore exploit highly informative structural guidance, although the privileged per-item information does not establish what could have been learned from experience alone. These results suggest that memory design may affect where accumulated experience becomes useful, even when its average benefit is modest.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在程序化汉字书写任务上比较五种 agent 条件下 668 个条目的表现，检验从既往尝试累积的持久记忆（自由笔记、可复用代码库）是否以及如何提升新问题的首次成功率，并额外用目标专属结构监督做事后对比。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「记忆库设计 + 迭代改进」机制可供核查是否能迁移为 LVR 中跨轮推理状态的更新与经验积累方式，而「结构监督事后增益大、平均收益有限」也提示监督信息量与贡献分配的问题；但任务为文本/代码 agent，与内部 latent 状态的关系需人工判断。
